profile.what: India's dominant coal miner: 768 MT produced in FY26 (about 74-80% of domestic output, CARE), sold mostly to power utilities under long-term fuel supply agreements (FSAs) at notified prices, plus e-auctions at market-linked premiums. Seven coal-producing subsidiaries (ECL, BCCL, CCL, NCL, WCL, SECL, MCL) and a planning arm (CMPDI). ~49% of India's proven coal reserves.
profile.customers: ~79% of FY26 offtake to the power sector; operative linkages of ~617.7 MTPA with power plants at 31-Mar-2026; supply below 75% of the FSA quantity triggers penalties (care).
profile.ownership: Maharatna PSU under the Ministry of Coal; Government of India 61.13% after the May-2026 OFS (63.13% before).

shares.note: Equity capital Rs6,162.73 cr; unchanged since the 2019 buyback

fy26.note: Company EBITDA (Rs53,276 cr) = PBT + finance cost + D&A, i.e. it includes other income. Our EBITDA (Rs41,243 cr) excludes other income and JV share and includes the stripping activity credit, as ICICI Direct and PL do. FY25 is restated: from FY25 levies collected as principal are shown inside revenue (C&AG/auditor emphasis of matter on 'treatment of levies on coal production and sales as amounts collected in principal capacity'; note 16(8) CFS).

otherIncomeFY26.src: ar26 (consolidated note 12.2; MD&A for escrow interest and JV share)

treasuryMar26.itcToBeUtilised: Rs17,006 cr accumulated ITC after GST on coal rose to 18% from 22-Sep-2025; ~Rs8,000 cr used in FY26, rest expected in FY27 (care)
treasuryMar26.note: Brokers' cash: ICICI Rs56,761 cr (cash, bank balances and current investments). Mine-closure escrow deposits sit in other financial assets (escrow rose Rs2,251 cr in FY26: Rs1,638 cr deposited, Rs876 cr interest, Rs263 cr reimbursed).

salesMix._note: Rs per tonne. 'Ex' = excluding other charges (levies and recoveries passed through); 'Incl' = billing price including them. Q2FY26 and Q3FY26 prices were presented on a different (net-sales) basis and are left out; their volumes: Q2 FSA 147.42 / EA 15.37 / washed 3.22 MT, Q3 165.14 / 19.52 / 3.52 MT (Q2 = 9M less Q1 and Q3).

q1fy27.drivers: Materials +27% (diesel +Rs435 cr, explosives +Rs244 cr); contractual +11% (outsourcing +Rs784 cr); other expenses +14% (rates and taxes +Rs1,246 cr incl. Jharkhand mineral-bearing land cess, passed through in billing); inventory drawdown Rs1,418 cr as pithead stock fell 28.9 MT to 101.4 MT; other income +26% (deposit interest +Rs449 cr). BCCL turned to a Rs68 cr loss.

history.event: Listed on NSE and BSE on 4-Nov-2010 (Government sale of shares)
Buybacks cut equity capital from Rs6,316 cr to Rs6,207 cr and then Rs6,163 cr (616.27 crore shares)
Government OFS (retail portion subscribed 1.4x; Business Standard 2-Jun-2023); Government holding 63.13% from then to Mar-2026
NCWA-XI wage pact (19% minimum guaranteed benefit, 25% allowance rise) for 1-Jul-2021 to 30-Jun-2026
BCCL IPO: Coal India sold 46.57 crore shares (10%) at Rs23 (Rs1,071 cr); listed 19-Jan-2026 at ~97% premium; subscribed ~144x
CMPDI IPO: OFS of 10.71 crore shares at Rs163-172; listed 30-Mar-2026 at Rs162.80 (subscribed ~1x)
Government OFS of 2% (base 1% + green shoe 1%) at Rs412 floor, ~10% below market; non-retail 8.1x subscribed
MCL files DRHP (1-Sep-2026): Coal India to sell 66.18 crore shares (10%); SECL listing planned in FY27

board.note: One independent director against SEBI LODR's requirement of half the board; appointments rest with the Ministry (AR FY26 corporate governance report).

liabilities.note: Supreme Court verdict (states may tax mineral rights and mineral-bearing land, retrospectively): management estimates Rs31,591 cr since 2005, of which ~Rs6,000 cr net after recovery from FSA customers (care). Executive pay-scale upgradation: CARE and the Q3 deck say Rs2,201 cr expensed in Q3FY26; the AR's MD&A cites a Rs1,458 cr provision (Jabalpur High Court order of 7-Jan-2026, retrospective from 23-Aug-2023) - see conflicts.

dividendPolicy: CPSE capital-restructuring guidelines (DIPAM): at least 30% of PAT or 4% of net worth, whichever is higher. Coal India paid Rs26.50 a share for FY26 (52.5% of EPS), Rs26.50 for FY25 (46%), Rs25.50 for FY24 (42%).
